mainTopic: The court's silent condition (לב בית דין מתנה) on communal offerings: rare cases, the פרה אדומה, and the מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and the חכמים
overview: This amud continues a back-and-forth between אביי and רבה about לב בית דין מתנה, the idea that the court silently sets a condition on communal animals. Under that condition, animals that turn out to be unneeded have only money-holiness and can be redeemed without a blemish. אביי asks why lost goats of the communal idol-worship offering must wait for a blemish. רבה answers that the court only makes conditions for common cases, and lost animals are rare. אביי points to the פרה אדומה, which is rare but can be redeemed. רבה first says the פרה is only בדק הבית property, but that answer is knocked down using רבי שמעון and ריש לקיש. רבה then says the פרה is an exception because it is so expensive. The גמרא explains that a dead פרה is redeemed for its hide, since even a small part of something so valuable is worth saving. אביי then objects from רבי שמעון's ruling on switching goats between days. רבה answers that רבי שמעון rejects the court's condition, while the חכמים accept it, as shown by the case of leftover תמידין. The גמרא begins asking who those חכמים are, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Lost goats of the idol-worship offering: die, or graze until blemished
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: goats for communal idol worship that got lost and were replaced must die according to רבי יהודה. ר' אלעזר and ר' שמעון say they graze until blemished, are sold, and the money goes to gift offerings, because a communal חטאת is never left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same goes for the goats brought for the community's mistaken idol worship. If they got lost and others were set aside in their place, all of the lost ones are left to die, says רבי יהודה. ר' אלעזר and ר' שמעון say: they graze until they get a blemish, then they are sold and the money goes to gift offerings, because a communal חטאת is not left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the ברייתא that אביי quoted. It is setting up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is in the opinion of ר' אלעזר and ר' שמעון: the animals must wait until they get a blemish before they can be sold. That suggests they still have full body-holiness (קדושת הגוף). אביי will use this detail to challenge רבה's idea of an unspoken court condition.

keyTerms.meaning: Goats brought as a communal חטאת for idol worship the community did by mistake
They are left to die (not sacrificed and not used)
They graze until they develop a blemish
Voluntary gift offerings (here, communal ones bought with the money)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ברייתא starting here. It is the end of a ברייתא quoted just before this, which is why it opens with "וכן" ("and likewise").

phrases.english: And likewise, goats of idol worship
that were lost, and he set aside others in their place,
all of them shall be left to die.
phrases.notes: He means the lost ones, if they are found later. The replacements were already offered.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
They should graze until they become blemished,
and they are sold, and their money goes to gift offerings.
Because a communal sin-offering is not left to die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא אביי was quoting before this section.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבה's rule of לב בית דין מתנה applies to lost communal offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: ר' אלעזר and ר' שמעון require waiting for a blemish

steps.title: Why not say the court's unspoken condition applies here?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: why wait for a blemish? The court's unspoken condition should make these animals redeemable right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why do they need to wait? Let's say the court silently made a condition about them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה using the ברייתא. If the court always sets a silent condition, these unneeded goats should be redeemable right away, without waiting for a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's rule says that when communal animals turn out to be unneeded, the court's condition gives them only money-holiness, so no blemish is needed. Yet ר' אלעזר and ר' שמעון do require a blemish. That seems to show no such condition was made.

keyTerms.meaning: The court's heart makes a condition: a silent stipulation the court has in mind

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main test of רבה's principle: does the silent court condition cover every communal animal that ends up unneeded?

phrases.english: But why?
phrases.notes: Why should they have to wait until they get a blemish?

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא לֵב בֵּית דִּין מַתְנֶה עֲלֵיהֶן!
phrases.english: Let us say the court has a silent condition on them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? לֵימָא לֵב בֵּית דִּין מַתְנֶה עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא in step 1 to attack רבה's principle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's principle of לב בית דין מתנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the court's condition applied, no blemish would be needed. The ברייתא requires one, so the condition seems not to exist.

steps.title: Lost animals are different because they are rare
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that lost animals are an uncommon case, and the court does not make conditions for rare situations.
steps.simpleTranslation: You're bringing a proof from lost animals? Lost animals are different, because that doesn't happen often.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his rule by limiting it. The court only plans ahead with a silent condition for things that happen often.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court's condition covers common cases, like leftover daily-offering animals. Losing an animal is rare, so the court didn't think about it in advance. That is why the lost goats keep full holiness and need a blemish.

phrases.english: Are you speaking about lost animals?
Lost animals are different, because they are not common.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבוּדִין קָאָמְרַתְּ? שָׁאנֵי אֲבוּדִין, דְּלָא שְׁכִיחִי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the principle to common cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The court's condition applies to every unneeded communal animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition only covers common situations, and losing animals is rare.

steps.title: The פרה אדומה is rare, yet it can be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to the פרה אדומה. It is rare, yet a ברייתא says it can be redeemed for any problem, even just because a nicer one was found. Only after it is properly slaughtered on its woodpile can it no longer be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the פרה אדומה, which is not common, and a ברייתא teaches: a פרה can be redeemed for any problem it has. If it died, it is redeemed. If it was slaughtered, it is redeemed. If a nicer one was found, it is redeemed. Once it was slaughtered on its woodpile, it can never be redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבה's answer with a case that is rare but still seems to involve a court condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A perfectly good פרה can be redeemed just because a nicer one turned up. אביי assumes this works because of the court's silent condition. If so, the court makes conditions even in rare cases, which knocks down רבה's answer in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: The פרה אדומה, the red heifer
Can be redeemed (its holiness moved onto money)
Its arrangement, the pile of wood where it is slaughtered and burned

phrases.english: But look at the heifer, which is not common,
and it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: פָּרָה נִפְדֵּית עַל כׇּל פְּסוּל שֶׁבָּהּ –
phrases.english: A heifer may be redeemed for any disqualification it has:
if it died, it shall be redeemed;
if it was slaughtered, it shall be redeemed;
phrases.notes: He means slaughtered in the wrong place, not on its proper woodpile.

phrases.english: if he found another one nicer than it, it shall be redeemed.
If he slaughtered it on top of its woodpile,
it can never be redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer that the court makes no conditions in rare cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the court does not make conditions for rare cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פרה is rare, yet it can be redeemed when a nicer one is found. That suggests the court makes a condition even in rare cases.

steps.title: The פרה is different: it is only holy for Temple upkeep
steps.stepSummary: רבה rejects the proof. The פרה אדומה is holy only as בדק הבית property, so it can always be redeemed, with no court condition needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פרה is different, because it counts as something holy for Temple upkeep.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה shows that the פרה case proves nothing about court conditions, because the פרה is redeemable for a completely different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Items holy for בדק הבית have only money-holiness from the start, so they can always be redeemed. The פרה's redemption comes from its own category, not from any silent court condition. רבה's rule that the court only plans for common cases stays standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Items made holy for Temple upkeep, which have only money-holiness
Money-holiness: the holiness rests on the item's value, so it can be redeemed

steps.whatToRemember: רבה holds that the court makes silent conditions only for common situations. Lost offerings are rare, so they keep full holiness. For now, רבה explains the פרה אדומה as בדק הבית property, but the גמרא knocks this answer down, and in step 10 רבה gives a new reason: the פרה's high price.
steps.confusionAlert: The פרה is still a holy, sacred item. The point is only that its kind of holiness is money-holiness (בדק הבית), so redeeming it is normal, even while it has no blemish.

phrases.english: The heifer is different,
because it is something made holy for Temple upkeep.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה, דְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פרה in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the פרה אדומה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פרה's redemption comes from its בדק הבית status, not from a court condition, so it says nothing about rare cases.

steps.title: How can a dead heifer be redeemed without standing and valuation?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה's claim that the פרה is plain בדק הבית property. Redemption normally needs העמדה והערכה, and a dead or slaughtered animal cannot be stood up and valued.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how can the פרה be redeemed after it died or was slaughtered? Redemption requires standing the animal up and valuing it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's last answer. If the פרה is only בדק הבית holiness, there is a problem: the ברייתא says it can be redeemed even after it died, and a dead animal cannot go through the redemption process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming a holy animal normally means standing it before a כהן so he can value it (העמדה והערכה). A dead or slaughtered animal cannot stand. So simple בדק הבית holiness cannot explain how the ברייתא allows redemption in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if what you just said is true
Standing: placing the animal before a כהן
Valuation: the כהן setting its price for redemption

phrases.english: If so,
if it died or was slaughtered, can it be redeemed?!
But we require standing and valuation!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:11–12. The animal has to stand before a כהן to be valued, and a dead animal can't stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מֵתָה אוֹ נִשְׁחֲטָה תִּפָּדֶה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the פרה is simple בדק הבית holiness that can always be redeemed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redemption requires העמדה והערכה. A dead or slaughtered animal cannot go through that process, so plain בדק הבית holiness cannot explain the ברייתא's ruling.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who exempts בדק הבית items from standing and valuation
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. In his view, only altar-consecrated items need העמדה והערכה, while בדק הבית items do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון's. He says altar-consecrated items needed standing and valuation, but בדק הבית items did not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends himself by saying the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. According to רבי שמעון, בדק הבית items do not need to be stood up and valued at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון limits העמדה והערכה to קדשי מזבח. Since the פרה is בדק הבית holiness, it can be redeemed even when dead, so רבה's position still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Items consecrated to be offered on the altar

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Shimon's,
who says:

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה,
phrases.english: items consecrated for the altar were included in standing and valuation,
but items consecrated for Temple maintenance
were not included in standing and valuation.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ברייתא to a specific תנא (רבי שמעון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every redemption requires העמדה והערכה, so a dead פרה could not be redeemed
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון, בדק הבית items need no העמדה והערכה, so a dead פרה can be redeemed

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא says a properly slaughtered heifer can never be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to the end of the same ברייתא: once the פרה is slaughtered on its woodpile, it can never be redeemed. He is setting up the claim that this does not fit רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, look at its end clause: once he slaughtered it on its woodpile, it can never be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tests רבה's answer by quoting the last line of the ברייתא. This sets up his next move, where he will show that רבי שמעון does not hold this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one part of a ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, the rest of it should follow him too. So the end clause, which forbids redemption after a proper slaughter, must also match רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the end clause: look at the last part of the source
Its woodpile: the wood arranged for burning the פרה

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Shimon,
say the end clause:
once he slaughtered it on its woodpile,
it can never be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end clause of the ברייתא must also match רבי שמעון, and the next step will show that it does not.

steps.title: ריש לקיש says רבי שמעון allows redeeming the heifer even on its woodpile
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון says the slaughtered פרה can become impure as food, because it had a time when it was fit. ריש לקיש explains that רבי שמעון holds the פרה can be redeemed even on its woodpile. That contradicts the end clause of the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught that רבי שמעון says the פרה can become impure with food impurity, since it once had a time of fitness. And ריש לקיש said: רבי שמעון used to say the פרה can be redeemed even on its woodpile!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי proves that רבי שמעון disagrees with the end clause. According to ריש לקיש, רבי שמעון holds the פרה can be redeemed even after it is slaughtered on the woodpile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food impurity applies only to something that was once fit to eat. ריש לקיש explains that the פרה counts as fit because it could still be redeemed on its woodpile and then eaten. That means the ברייתא's line 'never redeemed after slaughter' cannot be רבי שמעון's, so רבה's answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity that applies to food
A time when it was fit, here meaning fit to be eaten

phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
the heifer can become impure with the impurity of food,
since it had a time when it was fit;
phrases.notes: A time when it could have been eaten. ריש לקיש explains next how that could be.

phrases.english: and Reish Lakish said:
Rabbi Shimon used to say,
the heifer can be redeemed on its woodpile!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קשיא of step 8 by proving רבי שמעון disagrees with the end clause
steps.raayaObject: That the end clause of the ברייתא cannot follow רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about food impurity of the פרה, as explained by ריש לקיש

steps.title: The heifer is different because it is very expensive
steps.stepSummary: רבה changes his answer. The court does make a condition for the פרה even though it is rare, because the פרה is so valuable. Lost goats are not like that, so his rule about rare cases still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פרה is different, since it is very expensive.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives up the בדק הבית explanation. He agrees the court makes a condition for the פרה, but he says the reason is its high price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule from step 3 stays in place: the court does not make conditions for rare cases. The פרה is an exception, because losing such a costly animal would be a big loss, so the court makes a condition for it anyway. The lost goats are not that valuable, so they still have to wait for a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: dropping the earlier answer for a new one

steps.whatToRemember: The court does not normally make conditions for rare cases, so lost goats must wait for a blemish. The פרה אדומה is an exception: because it is so expensive, the court makes a condition for it even though it is rare.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבה is still saying the פרה is only בדק הבית holiness. That answer was knocked down. His new reason is the פרה's high price.

phrases.english: Rather, the heifer is different,
phrases.notes: So רבה now agrees the court does make a condition for the פרה, even though it's rare.

phrases.english: since its value is high.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה, הוֹאִיל וְדָמֶיהָ יְקָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from steps 5 and 7 with a new explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the high price creates an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פרה can always be redeemed because it is only בדק הבית holiness
steps.terutzMaskana: The court makes a condition for the פרה despite its rarity because of its great value; this does not apply to lost goats

steps.title: Why redeem a dead פרה if only dogs can eat it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that a פרה אדומה that died may be redeemed, and asks what the point is, since a dead animal's meat is only fit for dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: if the פרה died, it is redeemed. But do we redeem holy things just to feed them to dogs?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the ברייתא about the פרה אדומה and questions it. If the animal died, why bother redeeming it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that died without proper slaughter is נבלה, and its meat is only good for dogs. Redeeming holy property to take something that worthless seems pointless. So why would the court have made a condition that allows this redemption?

keyTerms.meaning: We redeem, meaning we transfer the holiness onto money

phrases.english: The Master said: If it died, it shall be redeemed.
phrases.notes: This is the פרה אדומה from the ברייתא quoted earlier.

phrases.english: But do we redeem consecrated items
in order to feed them to dogs?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי פּוֹדִין אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה said the court makes a condition for the פרה, the גמרא examines the ברייתא's line about a dead פרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redeeming holy property only to feed it to dogs makes no sense, so there seems to be no reason for this redemption.

steps.title: It is redeemed for its hide
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא answers that the dead פרה is redeemed for the sake of its hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: it is redeemed because of its hide.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא answers the question. The meat may be worthless, but the hide can still be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the פרה is redeemed, its hide becomes ordinary property and can be used for leather. So the redemption does have a real purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of, for the sake of

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said: Because of its hide.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a real benefit that justifies the redemption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Redemption would only be for meat that dogs eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The redemption is worthwhile because of the hide.

steps.title: Would the court make a condition just for a hide?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the court would really bother making a condition only to save the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the court really stand and make a condition with the hide in mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב משרשיא. A hide seems too small a thing for the court to plan a condition around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The redemption only works if the court made a condition ahead of time. It sounds strange that the court would plan such a condition just to rescue a skin.

keyTerms.meaning: With in mind, for the sake of

phrases.english: And does the court stand and make a condition
with the hide in mind?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָיְימִי בֵּית דִּין וּמַתְנוּ אַדַּעְתָּא דְּעוֹרָהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: רב משרשיא's answer that the redemption is for the hide
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hide is of small value, so it is unlikely the court would make a condition just for it.

steps.title: From a camel, even its ear
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא quotes a saying: from something very valuable, even a small part is worth saving. The פרה is so expensive that even its hide matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: as people say, from a camel, even its ear.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא defends the hide answer with a popular saying. When something is very valuable, even a small piece of it is worth keeping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרה אדומה is extremely rare and expensive, so its hide is also worth a lot. That makes it worth a condition by the court. This fits רבה's point in step 10 that the פרה's great value is what leads the court to make a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: People say: introduces a popular saying

steps.whatToRemember: A dead פרה אדומה is redeemed for its hide. Because the animal is so valuable, even its hide is worth a condition by the court.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: People say:
From a camel, its ear.
phrases.notes: He means that from something as valuable as a camel, even the ear is worth taking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי: מִגַּמְלָא אוּנַּהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-evaluates the value: a small part of a precious item is precious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hide is too minor for the court to make a condition about.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hide of a פרה אדומה is valuable enough to be worth a condition.

steps.title: אביי brings רבי שמעון's ruling on switching goats
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the משנה where רבי שמעון allows goats set aside for one day to be offered on another, because all of them atone for the same kind of sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: they asked רבי שמעון, may these goats be offered in place of each other? He said yes. They said: since their atonement is different, how can they be offered? He said: all of them come to atone for impurity of the מקדש and its holy foods.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a source to object to רבה's idea that the court makes a condition on public offerings. This step sets up the source; the actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Goats are set aside for specific days, such as ראש חודש, רגלים or יום כיפור. רבי שמעון lets a goat for one day be used on another day, and his reason is that they all atone for the same thing. Notice what reason he gives, because that is where אביי's question will come from.

keyTerms.meaning: This one in place of that one
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while impure

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: They said to Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: אביי is objecting to רבה here. The source is the משנה at the start of the מסכת.

phrases.english: What is the law, may they be offered this one in place of that one?
phrases.notes: They mean goats that were set aside for different days.

phrases.english: He said to them: They may be offered.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין כַּפָּרָתָן שָׁוָה,
phrases.english: They said to him: Since their atonement is not the same,
how can they be offered?
He said to them: All of them come to atone
for impurity of the Temple and its holy foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבה's claim that the court makes conditions on public offerings and brings a source against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's principle that the court makes a condition on public offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up the source. רבי שמעון explains the switch with a shared atonement instead of a condition by the court.

steps.title: Why not just say the court made a condition?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks why רבי שמעון needed the shared-atonement reason, when he could simply have said the court made a condition on the goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why give that reason? Let him say the court's mind makes a condition on them!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual attack. If the court always makes a condition, that would easily explain the switch, so why didn't רבי שמעון say so?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, the court silently makes conditions on public offerings. That would be the simplest reason a goat can move to another day. Since רבי שמעון gave a different reason, it looks like there is no such condition.

keyTerms.meaning: The court's mind silently makes a condition on them

phrases.english: But why? Let him say
the heart of the court makes a condition on them!
phrases.notes: Literally "the heart of the court". It means a condition the court has in mind without saying it out loud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? לֵימָא לֵב בֵּית דִּין מַתְנֶה עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the challenge from the source quoted in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's principle of לב בית דין מתנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the condition existed, רבי שמעון would have used it as his simple reason. His silence suggests it does not exist.

steps.title: רבי שמעון doesn't hold of the court's condition
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that this source is רבי שמעון, and רבי שמעון does not hold of לב בית דין מתנה. So it is no challenge to the חכמים, whose view רבה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are quoting רבי שמעון? רבי שמעון does not hold that the court makes a condition on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה deflects the challenge. The source belongs to רבי שמעון, who rejects the court's condition, so of course he gave a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question only works if everyone accepts the court's condition. רבה says this is a מחלוקת: רבי שמעון rejects the idea and the חכמים accept it. So רבה's principle still stands according to the חכמים.

phrases.english: You are quoting Rabbi Shimon?
Rabbi Shimon does not hold
that the court's mind makes a condition on them.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to one תנא who disagrees with the principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone holds the court makes a condition, so רבי שמעון should have used it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון rejects the condition, while the חכמים accept it.

steps.title: Proof from leftover תמידין
steps.stepSummary: רבה proves his claim through רבי יוחנן: unneeded תמידין cannot be redeemed while unblemished according to רבי שמעון, but they can according to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב עמרם in the name of רבי יוחנן: תמידין the public didn't need are not redeemed while unblemished according to רבי שמעון. According to the חכמים they are redeemed even while unblemished.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings proof that רבי שמעון rejects the court's condition. It comes from a מחלוקת about lambs for the תמיד that were left over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unblemished animal holy for the altar normally cannot be redeemed. The חכמים allow it here, which only makes sense if the court made a condition that the lambs would not become fully holy if they were not needed. רבי שמעון forbids it, which shows he does not accept that condition.

keyTerms.meaning: Lambs for the daily offering (קרבן תמיד)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse תְּמִידִין (daily-offering lambs) with תְּמִימִים (unblemished). Both words appear in this line.

phrases.english: As Rav Idi bar Avin said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Amram said, Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Daily-offering lambs that were not needed by the public,

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֵין נִפְדִּין תְּמִימִים,
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Shimon, are not redeemed while unblemished;
according to the Sages, they are redeemed while unblemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין, אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim of step 17 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון rejects לב בית דין מתנה and the חכמים accept it
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's report of the מחלוקת about unneeded תמידין
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole idea of לב בית דין מתנה as a clear מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and the חכמים.

steps.title: Who are the חכמים who argue with רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the opinion of the חכמים who accept the court's condition is found, and begins to suggest the חכמים of the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים who disagree with רבי שמעון, who are they? If we say they are the חכמים of the incense...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which known opinion of the חכמים is meant here. It starts suggesting the case of leftover קטורת, and the discussion continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן spoke of "the חכמים" who argue with רבי שמעון, and the גמרא wants to find their recorded ruling. The first suggestion is the חכמים in the משנה about leftover incense. Whether that works is checked next.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense burned in the מקדש

phrases.english: And the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Shimon,
who are they?
If we say the Rabbis of the incense,
phrases.notes: This points to the משנה in שקלים about leftover incense. The sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַאן נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the חכמים's view mentioned in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The recorded source of the חכמים's opinion that the court makes a condition
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A first suggestion begins: the חכמים of the קטורת. It continues on the next amud.
